title: Vega OS implementation guide
lead: Trace the existing Kepler app from native media initialization to modular Player configuration, remote controls, subtitles and Analytics. Use the current screen and code to distinguish Vega integration from browser Web and Android Fire TV apps.

blocks.text: Connect the modular Player to Vega media
blocks.summary: Connect the modular Player to Kepler’s native media and video surface, preserving initialization order and session release across app state changes.

blocks.text: Vega uses the modular Bitmovin Web SDK inside Amazon’s Kepler runtime. It does not use bitmovin-player-react-native or the Android Player SDK. Kepler renders the app’s React Native components, while @amazon-devices/react-native-w3cmedia provides the native media object and video surface. Keep the Vega-specific Player release pinned by apps/vega/package.json; the official sample declares a separate supported release channel from the general browser Player.

blocks.title: Display language
blocks.text: Use the app language selector to switch between English and Japanese. This guide uses captures from the English app. SDK identifiers, code and returned data retain their original spelling. Subtitle language belongs to the content and is selected separately from the application language.

An SDK is the library and interfaces used to integrate the Player; an API is a public configuration, operation or event exposed by that library. HLS and DASH are streaming formats that can offer several qualities; VOD means on-demand media with a fixed timeline. WebVTT is a text subtitle format with timed cues. DRM controls access to protected media and needs a compatible license service.
Prepare the Kepler host and native surface

items: Build and launch the existing Kepler host following Build the Kepler application in the Vega README linked below. Its identifier is com.playerlab.vega and its main component is com.playerlab.vega.main. Refresh the generated ignored runtime configuration before rebuilding when licenses change.

Follow src/App.tsx: it retains the applied PlayerConfig and SourceConfig and passes them to the Lab component BitmovinPlayer. A separate editable draft prevents incomplete form input from changing playback.

Follow src/BitmovinPlayer.tsx: KeplerVideoSurfaceView reports a native surface handle. Only an active app and current surface can start a session. The host first waits for the previous session’s release.

items.label: Vega README: build the Kepler host

blocks.text: The TextInput editors use Vega’s OS keyboard for remote text entry. manifest.toml requests com.amazon.inputmethod.service so that keyboard can open on Vega Virtual Device and hardware.
Initialize native media and manage its lifecycle

items: Follow src/playerSession.ts: initialize VideoPlayer, attach the surface, install the media adapters, create the modular SDK Player, bind observers, then load SourceConfig. Preserve this sequence when reusing or extending the host.

blocks.title: Initialize native media before constructing and loading the SDK Player

blocks.text: startVegaSession and createVegaPlayer are Lab helpers. VideoPlayer.initialize/setSurfaceHandle are Amazon media APIs; Player.addModule, new Player and Player.load belong to the Bitmovin Web SDK. The callbacks in the excerpt supply the actual constructors, observers and controller from BitmovinPlayer.tsx. This is a fragment of the existing host, not a complete standalone player.

blocks.title: Create the modular SDK Player without a browser container

blocks.text: vegaPlayer.ts registers the ReactNative media integration together with the format, renderer, adaptation, subtitle, DRM and related modules used by this app. polyfills.ts connects Amazon’s MediaSource, HTMLMediaElement and WebCrypto, plus XML parsing and Base64 helpers. A polyfill is compatibility code for a runtime API expected by the Web SDK; it does not create a browser document or HTML controls. The session-owned gvideo points the SDK at the current native VideoPlayer.

When the app moves to the background, the host releases native media before suspension. Returning to the foreground starts a replacement session with the retained configuration and source; it does not restore the previous position. A replacement waits for the previous owner’s release before using the global media adapters.
Change PlayerConfig and SourceConfig
blocks.summary: Map inputs to the Web SDK’s PlayerConfig and SourceConfig, keep Fetch transport and apply typed settings through the current native session.

blocks.text: Vega uses the Web SDK’s configuration names. PlayerConfig includes playback, buffer and adaptation; SourceConfig selects hls, dash or progressive. The Lab function parseConfiguration builds the basic objects, while VegaSessionApi.prepare materializes the additional typed values and approved functions before player creation and source loading. A property existing in the Web SDK declaration does not establish that the corresponding browser integration is available in this native host.
Map the basic configuration fields

blocks.title: Map basic playback, buffer and bitrate inputs

rows: Autoplay and startup mute
PlayerConfig.playback.autoplay / muted
Turn Autoplay off, Apply, then explicitly call play from SDK experiments. A startup flag and a runtime command affect different points in the session.
Audio/video buffer targets
PlayerConfig.buffer.audio.forwardduration / video.forwardduration

Try a positive value such as 10 seconds for one media type. Blank leaves the SDK default of 40 seconds per media type. The live playlist or rewind window can limit the effective forward buffer; compare actual playback and buffer state with the chosen content/device.
Adaptive video bitrate cap
PlayerConfig.adaptation.bitrates.maxSelectableVideoBitrate
Try 1500000 bit/s on a source with several representations. Read the selected quality and compare playback; this cap cannot add a representation absent from the source.
Media address
SourceConfig.hls / dash / progressive
The basic form emits the selected format key. For progressive it uses the string URL form. Match source format, container and codecs to the target’s capabilities.
Title, poster and position
SourceConfig.title / poster / options.startOffset / startOffsetTimelineReference
Try 5 seconds from Start on VOD. Title/poster are passed as metadata; this Kepler screen does not include a poster-artwork renderer. End uses the end/live edge as its reference.
External WebVTT
SourceConfig.subtitleTracks
Supply URL, label and language, then enable the external subtitle on load or choose its ID with PlayerAPI.subtitles. The app draws plain cue text in a native overlay.

blocks.text: Build source data for the selected format

blocks.title: Map media format, subtitles and start options to SourceConfig

blocks.text: media is an app-created object containing exactly the selected hls, dash or progressive URL. The source object also holds the external subtitle’s lang/id/enabled values and initial-position options. These Web SDK property names differ from the React Native wrapper’s language/identifier/isDefault names. Apply uses the validated source, then the existing session loads it only after native media and its surface are connected.
Apply configuration through the native session

blocks.title: Keep Fetch as the native transport

blocks.text: vegaPlayerConfig always merges requestApi: Fetch into the supplied network configuration. The form rejects XHR before Apply because this host has no XHR media transport. Other network callbacks remain part of PlayerConfig.network. To try a callback, search its path in Show all SDK configuration, read the declared arguments and return type, enable Allow this callback and Apply. Editing alone does not run code. SDK callbacks run when invoked; approved JavaScript value factories run on Apply or Run and when the approved session is recreated. The code runs inside this app without a sandbox.

items: Open Show configuration, retain the baseline source and change one field. Apply and recreate player validates the complete draft, releases the old session, then creates a new one and reloads the source. Reset draft leaves playback alone.

For more properties, open Show all SDK configuration and search an exact PlayerConfig or SourceConfig path. The input editor supports declared scalar, enumeration, object, dictionary and list values. Add array items in order and complete required fields.

Use a suitable representation for the SDK type. Binary certificate fields accept hexadecimal or Base64 bytes; object-instance inputs require a current SDK resource rather than an arbitrary object literal. Approved JavaScript executes inside the app without a sandbox.

Open Show applied code after Apply. The output includes applied values and function bodies, using license/header placeholders. Removing an additional override restores the basic form value or SDK default. Changing source, config or additional inputs starts a replacement session; it does not retain the old playback position.

blocks.text: Additional typed values override the basic form after Apply. Removing an override restores the form value or SDK default. An advanced SourceConfig.subtitleTracks array replaces the single-track form. Object and list editors let required related fields be completed together before Apply. A declared property or accepted input does not establish that its feature works on the native media surface.

blocks.caption: Applied configuration shown by the existing Vega app. D-pad focus allows the code lines to scroll into view; there is no clipboard integration.

blocks.text: Customize the native layout and remote controls
blocks.summary: Change Kepler’s native layout, subtitle overlay and controls while keeping each action reachable by remote focus.

blocks.text: The Vega app has no browser-based bitmovin-player-ui. App.tsx starts with ui: false, places BitmovinPlayer above a ScrollView, and renders ControlPanel, SDK API experiments and ConfigurationPanel below it. The UI change points are these React Native components and their StyleSheets. Setting PlayerConfig.ui to true or copying a browser theme does not produce HTML controls in Kepler.
Change the native layout and subtitle overlay

blocks.title: Keep the native surface and render subtitle text over it

rows: Resize the video and panel areas
BitmovinPlayer styles.video uses height: 50%; its surface fills the parent. App’s root uses flex: 1.
Adjust the native view dimensions together with the remaining settings area. Retain the current surface callback and handle binding; screen size changes do not replace that media connection.
Change how the image fits
KeplerVideoSurfaceView receives scalingmode="fit".
Use the values supported by the installed Amazon surface API when changing this prop. Player source poster/title fields do not control this native surface’s layout.
Restyle subtitle text
BitmovinPlayer’s captions and cue styles set the native overlay position, color, background and font.
Edit those StyleSheet entries. This renderer shows plain cue text; it does not implement WebVTT layout, HTML styling or the browser subtitle settings menu.

blocks.caption: The existing Vega app draws an external WebVTT cue as native text over the video. The surrounding controls are Kepler components, not the browser Player UI.

blocks.text: Keep remote focus and control actions connected

rows: Change control layout
ControlPanel.tsx composes rows using the localized Button wrapper and the Allow DVR Switch. The wrapper renders a focusable Pressable, with consistent text size, spacing and focus borders.

Edit these rows or the shared button styles in localization.tsx. Keep onPress, disabled state and the native D-pad focus path connected. On the tested Vega SDK, disabled controls received focus even with focusable=false. Keep their disabled appearance and focus indicator visible, and verify that Select performs no action. The input editors use the same visible focus treatment.
Connect a control to playback
The existing Live edge button calls controllerRef.current?.goToLiveEdge(); seek buttons use the same current controller.
Use the active controller or current SDK session for an added action. Compare its event/state result; do not retain a Player resource from an earlier session.

blocks.title: Make a native switch reachable by remote focus
blocks.text:
<Switch
          focusable
          style={styles.toggle}
          accessibilityLabel="Allow DVR"
          value={dvrAllowed}
          onValueChange={(v) => {
            onDvrAllowedChange(v);
            controllerRef.current?.setTimeShiftEnabled(v);
          }}
        />

Use D-pad and Select on a device, or arrow keys and Enter on a Vega Virtual Device. In the current screen, native buttons provide actions and switches explicitly opt into focus. Keep code output and expandable editors reachable after layout changes, including items below the video. Amazon’s focus guide explains why the spatial relationship between controls affects navigation. A touch-oriented React Native layout is not automatically usable with a TV remote.
Try subtitles, SDK operations and HLS insertion
blocks.summary: Call the installed SDK, render native subtitle cues and try HLS insertion using content and device capabilities suited to each feature.

blocks.text: Run operations on the current SDK session

Show SDK API experiments exposes the installed PlayerAPI operations with typed arguments. Inspect current SDK API availability checks that a method exists without invoking it. Run Vega SDK API executes the selected call and reports its value or error. Start with getCurrentTime while media advances; a method existing or returning a constant is not playback verification. Manifest helpers also follow the loaded format: HLS track helpers require HLS, and DASH period helpers require DASH.

items: For audio, call PlayerAPI.getAvailableAudio and pass a returned track ID to PlayerAPI.setAudio. Compare PlayerAPI.getAudio with the audible output. For quality and buffer experiments, compare current values and playback after the operation. A source with one quality or one audio track cannot demonstrate switching.

For low-latency controls, use a suitable live stream and compare target/readback and actual behavior. On VOD, a setter may be accepted while latency remains zero. A registered module does not make every source or device support its feature.

blocks.text: lab.getPlayer() and lab.getSource() resolve the current session. Return the published SDK type and obtain native objects from a real SDK API; an object literal cannot create an SDK instance or an HTML container. Callback outcomes are logged without request payloads. PlayerAPI.off needs the same callback instance passed to on, so select that actual resource from the current SDK session. Event summaries are bounded and credential fields are redacted; callbacks from retired sessions are ignored.

blocks.caption: PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime executed during playback. Read the return value together with changing video frames and SDK events.

blocks.text: Render subtitle cues in native text

items: For external subtitles, configure a WebVTT URL, label and language and enable the track on load. After Apply, use PlayerAPI.subtitles.list and PlayerAPI.subtitles.enable with the track ID when needed. Play through a matching cue interval and inspect CueEnter/CueExit events.

blocks.title: Observe subtitle cues in the native text adapter

blocks.text: attachSubtitleDisplay is the app’s text renderer. It tracks active cue text, removes cues on CueExit, clears the overlay when subtitles are disabled and detaches its event callbacks on disposal. This is why configuring a track and rendering its cues are separate parts of the integration.
Handle insertion markers in HLS

items: For HLS interstitials, select a source that actually contains insertion markers and enable PlayerConfig.tweaks.enable_sgai_handling. PlayerAPI.sgai.list returns its schedule; getActiveAd is normally empty outside an insertion. Try skip only while applicable and compare AdStarted, AdSkipped, AdBreakFinished and playback.

blocks.text: SGAI means server-guided ad insertion: it follows markers in the HLS source, unlike client-side ad integration. If an insertion falls outside the media window, compare the source’s program date time with the insertion start time.

blocks.title: Content and device prerequisites
blocks.text: The app registers DRM/crypto and additional format modules, but does not thereby supply compatible encrypted media, licenses or decoding capabilities. The official Vega sample excludes the HTML Player UI and client-side ads and documents constraints on server-side ad content. Use this host’s SGAI flow only with appropriate HLS. Keep general Web, Android Fire TV and Vega feature expectations separate.
FAQ and troubleshooting
blocks.summary: Diagnose native surface, transport, lifecycle, subtitle and licensing issues without confusing Vega with a browser or Android Fire TV integration.

rows: Why do browser UI settings have no visible effect?

Kepler has no browser HTML control layer. Keep ui: false and change native components/styles. A DOM container, canvas/WebGL VR renderer, browser UI factory, Cast receiver or device sensor is not supplied by an extra configuration key. This native integration does not provide client-side advertising. A callback that needs a real HTML container cannot use a plain object. DRM still needs compatible content, a license service and device support.
Why does XHR fail?
The media adapter requires Fetch and the form rejects other transport choices. Retain vegaPlayerConfig and the installed native media/polyfill initialization.
Why is the video black before readiness?

The native VideoPlayer must initialize and receive the current surface handle before SDK creation/load. Inspect setup/source errors and confirm that the app is active and the surface callback has arrived. A successful JavaScript build alone does not establish a working native surface.
Why does Apply or returning from the background reset playback?
The app replaces the session and reloads the retained source/configuration. It does not restore playback position. Background handling releases native media before the app can be suspended.
What if cleanup is unconfirmed?

Inactive status means that the owner no longer accepts SDK calls; it does not report completion of native cleanup. Recreate Vega player waits for the existing cleanup barrier before starting another owner. Restart the app if native player release or initialization cancellation is unconfirmed. Repeated Apply cannot confirm release.
Why are subtitles configured but not drawn?

Enable the external track on load or select its current ID, use cue times that overlap playback and inspect CueEnter. The renderer handles plain cue text; browser-specific styling and layout need their own native implementation.
Why does a licensed build still reject the app?

Allowlist com.playerlab.vega on the license in use, regenerate the ignored runtime configuration and rebuild the package. Runtime configuration is embedded before App is evaluated; editing the root file alone does not update an installed package.
Can the general browser SDK or a mocked test prove Vega support?

No. Keep the Vega-specific dependency and compare the official limitations. Unit tests can check validation and ordering, while native build, remote interaction, video and feature behavior require the target runtime.

blocks.text: Analytics / Observability
blocks.summary: Configure the Vega collector and source labels, then find the corresponding playback sessions and metrics in Bitmovin Dashboard.

blocks.text: Configure collection and source metadata

vegaPlayer.ts registers the Analytics module. App.tsx adds analytics.key only when BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_LICENSE_KEY is configured, independently of the Player license. The final PlayerConfig and SourceConfig pass through VegaSessionApi.prepare, so Show all SDK configuration can also supply supported Analytics properties and source labels. Use PlayerConfig.analytics for collector configuration and SourceConfig.analytics for source-level metadata such as videoId, title or customData1.

blocks.title: Add the optional collector to the existing Player configuration

blocks.text: tweaks.app_id in this fragment identifies the Player app for licensing; it is not an Analytics content identifier. The constructor receives the optional collector key, while source metadata travels with the source loaded later. The API catalog follows the installed Vega SDK surface, which differs from the React Native wrapper’s analyticsConfig and analyticsSourceMetadata names. Do not copy one platform’s configuration path into the other.
Find playback sessions in Dashboard

items: Use a collector license authorized for the Vega app, choose a non-sensitive videoId or experiment label, Apply and start playback. If the key changed, regenerate runtime configuration and rebuild before this experiment.

Open Bitmovin Dashboard with the matching Analytics license and period. Filter the relevant content/app labels and inspect sessions, startup, rebuffering, bitrate and errors alongside the local SDK events. The app sends collection events; aggregate viewing and visualization normally happen in Dashboard.

Follow the shared Analytics chapters for metric definitions, query access and analysis. Keep account API credentials in a trusted server-side environment; the collector license does not grant account query access.
